summary: Well-executed, preregistered paired study that strictly used a shared_initial_candidate design to compare verifier-only acceptance versus verifier+single-repair on synthetic NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The archived execution and analysis artifacts largely support the reported near‑null primary result (baseline 249/250 vs guarded 250/250). The paper is scientifically valuable as a narrowly scoped, preregistered negative/near‑null result, but several manuscript clarifications and formal fixes are required before finalisation.
critical_issues: References not provided in a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata; manuscript currently lists DOI/arXiv identifiers rather than an IEEE-formatted References section (developer policy requires conventional IEEE references when metadata exists).

Disclosure Statement includes execution-log-level details and per-file/full-hash items (model-call counts and specific SHA256s) and reads like an inventory of artifacts; developer policy requires the Disclosure be concise and not duplicate execution logs or per-file hashes in ordinary prose.

Preregistration described multiple partitions (emulation, community, production-like) and a sim‑to‑real research question; the manuscript text does not unambiguously state that the confirmatory execution was limited to the synthetic/emulation partition. This can be read as implying a sim‑to‑real contrast was executed when it was not. That must be clarified.

The paper must explicitly and unambiguously state the consequences of the shared_initial_candidate design for the estimand and inference (i.e., that the paired contrast measures only the effect of deterministic validation+repair on the same initial LLM candidate and that initial-sampling variation could not contribute to between-condition differences). While the manuscript asserts shared_initial_candidate semantics were followed, an explicit, prominent statement about the estimand and its practical consequence is required.

A minor but potentially confusing provider-call audit entry appears in the archived manifest (condition_counts: {"shared":250, "guarded":1}). The Methods should clarify the meaning of provider_call_audit fields (shared_initial_generation vs per-condition generation counts) so readers cannot misinterpret the run as generating distinct first-pass outputs per condition.
required_revisions: Replace the current cited_record_ids list with a conventional IEEE numbered References section containing full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv) for every cited work. Ensure each numbered citation in the text maps to a full IEEE reference and that each referenced work legitimately supports the proximate claim (no metadata-only or identifier-only entries). Use the archived reference-verification records to populate the bibliography; this is resolvable from supplied artifacts.

Condense the Disclosure Statement so it is concise and does not duplicate execution logs, per-file inventories, provider-call counts, or full artifact hashes in the paper body. Keep essential disclosures required by the track (models used and identifiers, autonomy-lock statement, preregistration identifier and its SHA-256). Move detailed manifests/hashes and per-file provenance to the archived evidence bundle and cite that bundle (manifest path and/or manifest SHA) rather than embedding them in the Disclosure text.

Explicitly state in Methods (and repeat in Results/Discussion as needed) that the confirmatory execution was limited to the synthetic/emulation partition (i.e., the confirmatory N=250 paired intents were synthetic), and that community and production-like partitions were not executed in the confirmatory run. If the preregistration allowed exploratory partitions, mark those as unexecuted in the confirmatory run and cite the preregistration artifact. This is resolvable from the preregistration and execution manifests.

Add one clear, short paragraph in Methods that explains the shared_initial_candidate design and its statistical implication for the primary estimand: that the same single initial LLM candidate was copied into baseline and guarded episodes for each intent, therefore any observed paired difference estimates only the marginal effect of validation+repair on an existing candidate (not differences due to initial-sampling across conditions). State explicitly that no independent first-pass generation per condition occurred and that initial-sample variation is not a between-condition source of variance. (Use the archived provider_call_audit and response paths to support the wording.)

Clarify the small-but-confusing provider_call_audit fields in a Methods footnote or short sentence (explain stage_counts, why model_calls_used=251 = 250 shared initial + 1 repair, and the semantics of the condition_counts entry) so readers cannot infer that distinct first-pass generations were produced per condition. This is a documentation clarification that can be resolved from the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifact.
optional_revisions: Provide (or point to in archived artifacts) the exact repair prompt/template text and a brief example repair exchange so readers can better interpret the single-repair policy and failure conversion mechanism (archived repair trace exists; include a short extracted example or path).

Add a short table in an appendix or in the archived artifacts mapping each main claim to the supporting citation(s) to aid reviewers/readers in verifying citation semantics (the run already contains a reference-verification record).

Include a brief note (or small supplementary figure) summarizing the exploratory per-vendor results if available in the archived artifacts; if not, state explicitly that per-vendor strata were not present in the confirmatory partition.

Replace the paired-bootstrap CI method with an explicit exact or Clopper–Pearson style paired-proportion confidence interval in a supplement or note (current bootstrap is acceptable but an exact interval would be a lightweight corroboration).
